name: Gerzeh meteoritic-iron beads
summary: Around 3200 BCE people at Gerzeh in Egypt hammered iron from meteorites into thin sheet and rolled it into beads, working iron long before iron was smelted from ore.
description: Meteoritic iron hammered into sheet and rolled into tubular beads; a metalworking route requiring no extraction of iron from ore.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.

date.label: by c. 3100 BCE
date.basis: Closed burials are assigned to Naqada IIC–IIIA, approximately 3400–3100 BCE; burial placement supports inferred use by the approximate end of that context, not a hard earliest manufacturing date.

events.statement: Hammered and rolled meteoritic-iron beads formed part of the burial assemblages in Gerzeh during the dated Naqada horizon.
events.population: People furnishing and wearing beads in the two Gerzeh burials
events.caveats: The beads were deposited in a broad dated horizon; deposition bounds an earlier manufacturing/use claim but does not fix its first date or show wider trade.

evidence.supports: Describes beads from closed burials, their manufacture and Naqada IIC–IIIA dating of approximately 3400–3100 BCE.
